   • Total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (removal of *both* ovaries is essential — contralateral GCT risk is low but not zero; also eliminates future estrogen source)  
   • Surgical staging: peritoneal washings, omentectomy, pelvic/para-aortic lymphadenectomy (though lymph node involvement is rare in early GCT and low-grade endometrioid cancer)  
   • Intraoperative assessment of the adnexal mass (frozen section if indicated, though final diagnosis requires permanent sections due to GCT’s subtle histology)

- PMB is never normal — timely evaluation was critical.  
- Two distinct but biologically linked cancers were identified — treatable with surgery.  
- Hormonal driver (ovarian tumor) explains the endometrial cancer — removal of the ovary resolves the underlying cause.  
- Lifelong surveillance (especially inhibin B) is required due to GCT’s unique natural history.
